clue.text: Remove top quickly and lose it

definitions.meaning: read literally, to flip a lid open is to whip the top off something fast
colloquially, to lose it is to lose one's temper and go berserk

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening a jar fast, with a warning not to drop the lid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for losing one's temper suddenly pictures the head's top flying off, so both senses match.

clue.text: Friends of the Earth's opponent?

parts.note: the green group's initials, F, O and E, spell a word for an enemy, so its opponent is its own abbreviation

explanation.walkthrough: The environmental campaign group Friends of the Earth abbreviates to the very word that means an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is an enemy, an opponent.

clue.text: Epic work I frequently read up without reaching the end

indicators.note: in a down clue, read up means the letters run bottom to top
without reaching the end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: daily means every day, frequently

explanation.surface: Someone often reads an epic but never finishes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without reaching the end' cuts DAILY to DAIL; 'read up' turns it to LIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is a classic epic work.

clue.text: Boys affected with it have little energy in reserve?

definitions.text: Boys affected with it have little energy in reserve?

indicators.note: in reserve means E is stored within the anagram
affected means the letters of boys and it are altered into a new order

parts.note: E is the short form of energy

explanation.surface: Boys with this condition carry stored energy as fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' signals the anagram and 'in reserve' the insertion. Read straight, the clue says obesity is stored energy, since body fat is energy held in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity means excess body fat, which is stored energy, so the clue defines it as a whole.

clue.text: Vehicle is in Le Mans a short time before event's over

parts.note: in French, spoken in Le Mans, is is est
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: over means the word for the event is turned backwards

parts.note: a race is a sporting event, as at Le Mans

explanation.surface: A car at the Le Mans race, briefly ahead before the event ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Le Mans' is a pointer to French, not a racing reference alone; 'over' signals the reversal and 'before' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a car with a rear load space, a vehicle.

clue.text: Reserve having to make effort on field having missed header

indicators.note: missing its header means the phrase loses its first letter

parts.note: play up, as in the poem's Play up and play the game, means try harder on the sports field

explanation.surface: A reserve player who missed a header while trying hard on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay up is to store away, put in reserve.

clue.text: Corrupt deputy's taken over party

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken over means sitting on top of the party word

parts.note: DEP is the abbreviation for deputy
a rave is a big dance party

explanation.surface: A deputy who has seized control of a party is corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprave is to corrupt morally.

clue.text: Story gone over in brief, oddly

indicators.note: something gone over has been turned back on itself, so the picked letters are read backwards
oddly signals taking the first, third and fifth letters of the word brief

explanation.surface: A tale that someone has gone over briefly, in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd letters of 'brief', B, I, F; 'gone over' turns them round. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A story, informally, is a lie, as in a child telling stories; a fib is a small lie.

clue.text: Established convention of one African country among many

indicators.note: among means the country goes amid the letters of the number

parts.note: forty stands loosely for many
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A custom shared by one African nation among many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is just 'a'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A formality is an established procedure or convention.

clue.text: Cotton maybe engulfed rayon at first as top seller

indicators.note: engulfed means the bandleader swallows the letter

parts.note: Billy Cotton was a famous British dance bandleader

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of rayon

explanation.surface: Cotton swamped rayon early on as the bestselling fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton' looks like the fabric, but it is Billy Cotton, a British bandleader of radio and TV fame. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand leader is the product that sells best in its market, the top seller.

clue.text: Dip during bad year, it would seem

indicators.note: during means the dip comes in the middle of the bad thing

parts.note: bad as a noun, wickedness, is evil
a dip in a surface is a dent

explanation.surface: A slump in the economy during a bad year, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sentence adverbs of appearance: evidently means apparently, as it would seem.

clue.text: At recreation area, a hoodie

parts.note: a park is a public area set aside for recreation

explanation.surface: Someone at a playground wearing a hooded top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket, so it is an example of a hoodie.

clue.text: Notice girl's dressed in pink daily, being a follower of fashion

indicators.note: the notice and girl are clothed in the newspaper, placed inside it

parts.note: the Financial Times, FT, is a daily paper printed on pink paper
a notice in a paper is an ad
Di is a short girl's name; with the 's it gives DIS

explanation.surface: A girl's announcement appears in the Financial Times, showing she follows fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddist follows each passing craze, so is a follower of fashion.

clue.text: Mixed fresh figs in snack

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the three words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A snack of fresh figs, mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish fingers are breaded fish strips, a quick snack or light meal.

clue.text: Notice pal going wild at club?

indicators.note: going wild means the letters of pal run riot into a new order

parts.note: a club is a playing card of one suit

explanation.surface: A friend running riot at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. 'going wild' turns PAL into PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a printed sign or poster, a public notice.

clue.text: Don't go eating a foreign dish

indicators.note: eating means the word for remaining takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: an appeal not to go is to stay

explanation.surface: A plea for someone to stay and eat a dish from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a Southeast Asian dish of skewered meat with peanut sauce, so a foreign dish.

clue.text: Keen worker at bottom of ditch

indicators.note: in a down clue, at the bottom means the worker comes below the ditch

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
an ant is a worker in the insect sense

explanation.surface: An eager labourer at the bottom of a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means sharp or incisive, and keen can mean sharp, as of a blade or wit.

clue.text: Sister spoken of as more serene figure of authority?

indicators.note: spoken of as means the two words for more serene and authority figure are said out loud

parts.note: more serene is calmer; a leading light is a figure of authority

explanation.surface: A nun described as a more tranquil leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, with the R silent, CALMER LIGHT sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carmelite nun belongs to the Carmelite order and is addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Foreigner missing top grade in exam, bouncing back

indicators.note: in means the shortened foreigner goes inside the exam

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken again

indicators.note: missing means the top grade letter is taken out

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner
A is the top grade

explanation.surface: A foreign student who failed to get an A recovers in a retake.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient means able to recover quickly, to bounce back.

clue.text: Complimentary drinks in these commercial zones

parts.note: complimentary means given free
port is a fortified wine, so drinks can be ports

explanation.surface: Free drinks are on offer in these trading zones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in these' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Free ports are areas where goods can be landed without customs duty, commercial zones.

clue.text: Scientist fails to finish page for document

indicators.note: fails to finish means the scientist's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Louis Pasteur was a French scientist

explanation.surface: A scientist doesn't complete a page of his paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paste-up is a layout document with text and pictures pasted on a board for printing.

clue.text: Made fun of counsellor speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the word for a counsellor is said out loud

parts.note: a guide is an adviser or counsellor

explanation.surface: Someone mocked a counsellor's way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy is to ridicule, so guyed is a past tense meaning mocked.

clue.text: Good to swindle American killer

parts.note: a ramp is British slang for a swindle
US means American

explanation.surface: A good con played on an American murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Grampus is an old name for the killer whale and also a related dolphin.

clue.text: Is in a small company that's struggling for capital

indicators.note: struggling means the letters are wrestled into a new order

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A small firm in financial difficulty, short of capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's struggling' shuffles ISINA with CO; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Like somewhere to sleep in town …

parts.note: as means like
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Looking for somewhere to stay in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. ASCOT is the Berkshire town known for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a town in Berkshire, England, home of Royal Ascot races.

clue.text: I hate Much Ado About Nothing

indicators.note: about means the word for fuss goes round the zero

parts.note: much ado is a fuss, and to be in a lather is to be agitated
O, shaped like zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone declares their dislike of Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic play title is broken up: 'Much Ado' is LATHER, 'About' wraps it round O, 'Nothing'. The definition is what one who detests would say.
explanation.definitionFit: A loather is one who detests, the kind of person who keeps declaring I hate this.

clue.text: … book into awful place, almost: this?

definitions.text: … book into awful place, almost: this?

indicators.note: into means the book goes inside the shortened awful place
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: hell is the most awful place
OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Booking into a dreadful place to stay in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Read on from 21-down: somewhere to sleep in town, booked into, a near hell: this is a description of a bad hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is somewhere you book into to sleep in town, as the run-on clue describes.

clue.text: Avoid central part of US state, heading east

indicators.note: central part of means the state name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Nevada is a US state

explanation.surface: Advice to skip the middle of a state while driving east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' is a link: E follows at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or escape something.

clue.text: Needlewoman known as a drama queen

definitions.meaning: the woman whose name is on the obelisk in London called her Needle
a queen in drama, the heroine of Shakespeare and Shaw plays

explanation.surface: A seamstress with a reputation for histrionics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needlewoman' looks like a seamstress, but it is the queen of Egypt, after Cleopatra's Needle, an obelisk on London's Thames embankment. 'drama queen' is literal: a queen in plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen gives her name to a London obelisk and is a stage queen in Shakespeare.

clue.text: A police inspector called up for help

indicators.note: in a down clue, called up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: Someone calls up a police inspector to ask for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to give aid is to assist, to help someone in need.

clue.text: Relaxed half the weekend

definitions.meaning: relaxed means rested in a chair, past tense of to sit
the weekend is Saturday and Sunday

explanation.definitionFit: To have sat down is to have relaxed, and Sat abbreviates Saturday, one weekend day.

clue.text: Prize fighting dog — pup, maybe — consumes a portion of food

indicators.note: consumes means the string of pieces takes the letter a inside

parts.note: pot is slang for a prize or trophy
the tosa is a Japanese breed of fighting dog
a pup is a cheeky young man, so a lad

explanation.surface: A champion fighting dog, a mere pup, eats a serving of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize fighting' suggests boxing, but splits as prize then fighting dog; the tosa is a Japanese fighting breed. 'consumes' puts A inside the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Potato salad is a dish served as a helping alongside a meal, a portion of food.
